post.description: Opens a local file by path. A .twb/.twbx opens as a workbook; a datasource file (Excel, text, spatial, extract, .tds, and the like) attaches to the open workbook, creating one if none is open. filePath must name an existing file: a missing file is rejected with 404 file-not-found and an extension Tableau cannot open with 400 unsupported-file-type, both before anything is dispatched. The extension is checked first: a missing file with an unsupported extension gets 400. A SUCCEEDED operation means the open command ran, not that the file finished loading; the product may show a dialog (for example a login or upgrade prompt), so check GET /v0/app/dialogs if the file does not appear. Opening a workbook while the open workbook is empty and unsaved replaces it in this window, and GET /v0/workbook then reports the opened workbook. Re-opening the file that is already open reloads it in place, prompting first to save unsaved changes. Opening any other workbook while one is open launches it in a NEW Desktop window, and this API session stays bound to the workbook it started with -- GET /v0/workbook continues to report the original.

post.description: Sets whether the Data Source page is the active tab, equivalent to clicking the Data Source tab or returning to a sheet tab. Activating it shows the workbook's active data source; deactivating it shows the sheet that was active before the Data Source page. Repeated requests for the same state have no additional effect. A published data source that cannot connect leaves the active tab unchanged and still succeeds, so read isDataSourcePageActive from GET /v0/app to confirm the switch. Fails when the active data source cannot be loaded. Leaving the page can finish creating a pending extract, which may open a dialog, so the response can be 202 until the dialog closes. The switch is recorded in undo history.

post.description: Refreshes the live data for the datasource resolved by {id} (its internal name from GET /v0/workbook/datasources), the way the toolbar Refresh Data Source does. Use refreshExtract to refresh an extract. For an OData datasource, the extract is refreshed instead. A credential prompt keeps the Operation RUNNING with blockingWindows; a connection failure outside the Data tab is shown in a Desktop error dialog and the Operation still ends SUCCEEDED. A cancellation reported by the refresh command ends as a CANCELLED Operation. A refresh requested while the workbook is committing is skipped and ends SUCCEEDED, even for an id that matches no datasource. Otherwise an id that matches no datasource returns 404 when the request completes synchronously; after a 202 response, the same rejection appears in the polled HTTP 200 Operation with state FAILED.

post.description: Replaces a single dashboard with the submitted Tableau XML, leaving the workbook's other sheets intact. A missing or empty body is rejected with 400 and a non-XML Content-Type with 415. A non-empty XML body that is not well-formed, that the product cannot load into a valid workbook, or that has a dashboard zone with type-v2='worksheet' is rejected with 422. The payload is NOT validated against the schema; use POST /v0/workbook/document:validate for XSD validation. This apply is unconditional last-writer-wins: it performs no precondition/If-Match check and will overwrite a concurrent edit to the same sheet. The apply is rejected with 409 when the submitted payload's sheet name does not match the target sheet's current name -- for example, if you renamed the sheet in the payload, or another editor renamed it after you read the document -- or when the name-matching payload element is the wrong sheet subtype (a story, <dashboard type='storyboard'>, where the target is a dashboard). A known client rejection found while the apply completes synchronously (409 or 422) returns a Problem Details response with code operation-failed carrying the underlying tableauErrorCode. An <add-in> whose extension-url is tableauunzippedpackagesrc:///<absolute folder path> registers that unzipped extension package for the session; a folder that does not exist fails the apply. Any other failure, including any failure of an apply that returns 202, is reported as a FAILED operation. An id that matches no sheet or resolves to a sheet of a different kind returns 404 when the apply completes synchronously.

Top-level <datasources> definitions in the payload are ignored, but the applied dashboard's datasource references must still resolve to a datasource already present in the open workbook -- a reference to an absent datasource is rejected with 409.

get.description: Renders a single dashboard (resolved by id) as an image, returned inline as base64 or written to a caller-supplied file path. The id must resolve to a dashboard: an id that matches no sheet returns 404, and an id that resolves to a non-dashboard sheet or to a dashboard that is not yet renderable returns 409. A 404 or 409 applies to a synchronous response: when the request settles after a 202 response, the same rejection appears in the polled HTTP 200 Operation with state FAILED, whose error carries the same code, plus tableauErrorCode for a 409.

parameters.description: The resource's stable id as returned in its list or GET response, not its display name or caption.

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: Path to write the image to. Must be absolute and name a file; a path with no file name (for example a trailing slash) or any '.'/'..' path segment is rejected with 400 invalid-query-parameter. The path is otherwise validated only when the image is written: a path whose parent directory does not exist or is not writable, or that names an existing directory, fails with 500 operation-failed and the Problem body carries the underlying tableauErrorCode. An existing file at the path is overwritten. When set, the response carries this path instead of inline base64; when omitted, the image is returned as base64.

parameters.name: mimeType
parameters.description: Requested image MIME type (e.g. image/png, image/jpeg, image/svg+xml). Defaults to image/png; an unsupported type also falls back to image/png. Aliases are canonicalized (e.g. jpg to image/jpeg); image/svg+xml must match exactly. The effective type is returned in the response.

ImageExport.description: The result of exporting a sheet as an image: exactly one of imageBase64 (the default) or filePath (when the filePath query parameter is supplied).

imageBase64.description: The encoded image bytes, standard base64 with padding (RFC 4648). Present when filePath was not supplied.

effectiveMimeType.description: The MIME type actually written. This may differ from the requested mimeType: an unsupported type falls back to image/png, and aliases are canonicalized (for example jpg to image/jpeg).

width.description: Size of the rendered raster image in pixels. -1 when effectiveMimeType is image/svg+xml, because vector output has no pixel size.

height.description: Size of the rendered raster image in pixels. -1 when effectiveMimeType is image/svg+xml, because vector output has no pixel size.

filePath.description: The filePath query value, echoed verbatim; the image was written there. Present only when filePath was supplied.

effectiveMimeType.description: The MIME type actually written. This may differ from the requested mimeType: an unsupported type falls back to image/png, and aliases are canonicalized (for example jpg to image/jpeg).

width.description: Size of the rendered raster image in pixels. -1 when effectiveMimeType is image/svg+xml, because vector output has no pixel size.

height.description: Size of the rendered raster image in pixels. -1 when effectiveMimeType is image/svg+xml, because vector output has no pixel size.

SummaryData.description: Tabular worksheet data as columns and rows. Returned by both the summary-data and underlying-data endpoints; the shape is identical for each.

columns.description: The table's columns, in the order the cells of each row appear.

name.description: Display caption of the column as shown in Tableau (for example SUM(Sales)). This is not the field name that columnsToIncludeByFieldName accepts.

dataType.description: Tableau data type of the column. cstring is a string column. Clients must tolerate values not listed here.

rows.description: One array per row, with one cell per entry in columns, in the same order. integer cells are JSON integers, real cells are JSON numbers, boolean cells are JSON booleans, and cstring cells are strings. date cells are strings formatted yyyy-MM-dd and datetime cells are strings formatted yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss[.SSS], both without a timezone. tuple and spatial cells are strings (a spatial cell is an opaque hash, not geometry). time, binary, table and unknown cells, and null values, are null. In a cstring column other special values appear as sentinel strings such as %all%; in other columns they are null. Values are the raw, unaliased, unformatted data values. Rows are truncated at the effective maxRows cap and the response carries no truncation flag, so if rows.length equals the cap more rows may exist. When there is no data, columns and rows are both empty. The row count comes from the first column, so rows is also empty when that column holds only time, binary, table or unknown values.

LogicalTableItem.description: A logical table available for a worksheet's data.

WorkbookValidationIssue.description: One issue found while validating a workbook document.

severity.description: error makes the document invalid; warning does not. Clients must tolerate values not listed here.

line.description: 1-based line of the offending element; omitted when unknown.

column.description: 1-based column of the offending element; omitted when unknown.

element.description: Tag name of the offending element; omitted when unknown.

ValidationResult.description: The outcome of validating a workbook document.

issues.description: Issues found in the document; empty when the document is clean.

ShowMeType.description: A serialized Show Me visualization type.

ShowMeRequest.description: The Show Me visualization to apply to a worksheet. showMeType must be one of the ShowMeType values; any other value is rejected with a 400. Prefer a type reported as applicable by GET /v0/workbook/worksheets/{id}/showMe for the same context.

dataSource.description: Optional internal datasource name used to resolve selected fields.

fieldsSelectedInSchemaViewer.description: Optional fully qualified encoded field names, each with at least a datasource and field component. An explicit empty array supplies an empty field selection; omission preserves ambient selection.

ShowMeOptions.description: Show Me options from Tableau's current native model for the worksheet and selected-field context, in native order. The set of options is fixed for the host (bar-measure is never offered; scatter-matrix is offered only when the host enables it); context changes only each option's applicability.

options.description: Every option offered by the current native Show Me model, in native order, including inapplicable options.

ShowMeWorksheet.description: The worksheet evaluated by the native Show Me model.

ShowMeOption.description: A visualization option from the current native Show Me model. showMeType is always a ShowMeType value accepted by POST /v0/workbook/worksheets/{id}:showMe.

isApplicable.description: Whether the native Show Me model can apply this option to the worksheet and selected fields.

vizHasRequiredFields.description: Whether the current visualization supplies the fields required by this option.

dataSourceHasRequiredFields.description: Whether the current datasource supplies the fields required by this option.

helpUrl.description: The help URL supplied by the current native Show Me model.

CalculatedFieldValidationError.description: A validation error in the calculated-field formula or its caption.

position.description: 0-based offset of the error in formula, in UTF-16 code units; 0 when the error is not tied to formula text.

length.description: Length of the error in UTF-16 code units; 0 when the error is not tied to formula text.

ValidateCalculatedFieldRequest.description: The formula, and optionally the caption, of a new or edited calculated field to validate on a datasource.

formula.description: The calculated-field formula text to validate.

caption.description: The caption the calculated field would have. A blank caption or one that matches another field's caption is reported as an error.

fieldName.description: The existing calculated field being edited, given as its internal name qualified by the datasource's internal name, in the form [datasource-name].[field-name] (e.g. "[federated.0abc123].[Calculation_123]"). The field keeps its own caption, and a formula that references the field itself, directly or through other calculations, is reported as a circular reference. A field that is not a calculated field in the datasource named by {id} is reported as an error. Omit to validate a new calculated field.

ValidateCalculatedFieldResponse.description: The outcome of validating a new or edited calculated field on a datasource.

isAggregate.description: Whether the formula aggregates, such as SUM([Sales]). Present only when isValid is true.

dataType.description: The data type the formula evaluates to, using the datatype values of a workbook <column> element. Present only when isValid is true. Clients must tolerate values not listed here.

SortRequest.description: The sort to apply to a field on the worksheet.

fieldName.description: The on-shelf field to sort, given as its field-instance name qualified by its datasource caption, in the form [Datasource Caption].[field-instance] (e.g. "[Sample - Superstore].[none:Ship Mode:nk]"). The base column name (e.g. "[Sample - Superstore].[Ship Mode]") will not match any field on the view and the sort is silently ignored. A value that is not bracketed (e.g. "Ship Mode") yields a FAILED operation.

direction.description: Sort direction; defaults to 'asc' when omitted. Only the listed values are accepted; any other value is rejected with a 400.

sortType.description: Sort type; defaults to 'data-source-order' when omitted. Only the listed values are accepted; any other value is rejected with a 400.

clearSort.description: When true, removes the existing sort on `fieldName` instead of applying one; `fieldName` is still required.

StartPageVisibility.description: Whether the Tableau Desktop start page is visible.

ToggleDataSourcePageRequest.description: Whether the Data Source page is the active tab.

filePath.description: Path to save the workbook to (Save As); must end in .twb or .twbx. Omit, or send an empty value, to save the workbook in place at its current path.

ExportAsWorkbookRequest.description: What to export and where to write it.

filePath.description: Path to write the export to. Must be absolute and name a file; a directory, a trailing slash, or any '.'/'..' path segment is rejected with a 400. Its extension must match format: .pdf for pdf, .pptx for powerpoint, .twbx for packaged-workbook, and .twb or .twbx for prior-version.

format.description: The export format that selects what file to produce. Only the listed values are accepted; any other value is rejected with a 400.

targetVersion.description: Required when format is prior-version: the customer-facing Tableau release to down-save to (e.g. "2024.1"). Ignored for other formats.

isFullRefresh.description: Force a full refresh instead of an incremental one. Defaults to false: incremental when the extract is configured for incremental refresh, otherwise a full refresh.

ApiRoot.description: API versions and the resource link map.

AppState.description: One app-wide point-in-time snapshot of Desktop activity and modal state. Window arrays are not attributed to an operation. When state is BLOCKED, blockedBy reports the strongest observed signal in precedence order: MODAL_DIALOG, the first active activity in canonical order, PROGRESS_DIALOG, MODAL_LOOP, then UI_UNRESPONSIVE.

state.description: IDLE only after a complete UI snapshot observes no activity, modal loop, or modal window; otherwise BLOCKED.

blockedBy.description: Present when state is BLOCKED and identifies the strongest observed signal.

uiSnapshotAvailable.description: Whether modal-loop and window evidence was captured within the bounded UI probe interval. A false value never produces IDLE and window arrays are omitted.

activeActivities.description: All active native activities in canonical order: LOADING, QUERYING, EXTRACT_REFRESH, DOWNLOADING, SERVER_COMMUNICATION.

CapabilityMatrix.description: Capabilities keyed on operationId. An operationId missing from the map is not part of this API version's public contract.

requiresServer.description: Whether a connected Tableau Server or Cloud session is required.

Health.description: Liveness probe result; returned only when the API is enabled.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed. The code field identifies the specific problem, such as a missing required header or an unreadable body.

Unauthorized.description: The bearer token was missing or invalid. The response carries a WWW-Authenticate challenge.

WWW-Authenticate.description: Bearer challenge with the realm and the resource_metadata URL of the OAuth protected-resource document.

Forbidden.description: The request origin was not permitted.

NotFound.description: The addressed resource does not exist. The code field distinguishes an unknown route from a valid resource with an unknown id.

MethodNotAllowed.description: The path exists but does not support this HTTP method.

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the current state of the workbook or the application. The code field identifies the specific conflict.

UnsupportedMediaType.description: The request Content-Type is not accepted by this endpoint.

MisdirectedRequest.description: The request Host header was not exactly 127.0.0.1:<port> or localhost:<port> for the bound port.

UnprocessableContent.description: The request was well-formed but semantically invalid and could not be applied, such as a document whose structure the product rejects. The code field identifies the specific problem.

ServiceUnavailable.description: The service is temporarily unavailable. The code field identifies the cause, such as api-disabled.

Accepted.description: The command did not settle within the synchronous window. The body is the pending operation; poll the Location URL until it reaches a terminal state. A rejection that settles after this response is reported by the poll as a 200 Operation with state FAILED, not as the 4xx or 500 status a synchronous response would carry.

Location.description: Relative URL of the operation to poll.

UserAgent.name: User-Agent
UserAgent.description: Identifies the calling client as an RFC 9110 product token, such as my-client/1.2.0. Requests without a non-empty User-Agent are rejected with missing-user-agent.
